From:            Alan Blind
To:              Petition Resource
Cc:              Dennis Galvin; PalisadesRestartProject
Subject:         [External_Sender] Supplement to 10 CFR 2.206 Petition – Palisades Seismic Reevaluation (T-81 Commitment and
                 Related Issues)
Date:            Thursday, April 2, 2026 5:42:51 PM
Attachments:     Seismic 2.206 Supplement.pdf




To:
Executive Director for Operations
U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
Email: Petition.Resource@nrc.gov


Dear NRC Executive Director for Operations,

I am submitting the attached supplement to my August 6, 2025 petition under 10 CFR § 2.206
regarding Holtec Palisades, LLC’s noncompliance with NTTF Recommendation 2.1 seismic
reevaluation requirements.

This supplement identifies a fundamental contradiction in the Palisades licensing basis related
to Tank T-81. The originally required modification to achieve HCLPF capacity greater than
RLGM was cancelled in 2016 based on the stated intent to use insights from a future Seismic
Probabilistic Risk Assessment (SPRA) to determine appropriate actions. However, in its
March 25, 2026 submittal, Holtec states that SPRA results will not be used to initiate
structural design changes. As a result, neither the original deterministic requirement nor the
replacement SPRA-based evaluation framework has been satisfied.

The supplement also provides updated information based on Holtec’s March 25, 2026
submittal and demonstrates that the issues raised in the original petition remain unresolved. In
addition to the T-81 issue, the supplement addresses:

       Holtec’s failure to demonstrate compliance with specific seismic performance
       commitments under 10 CFR § 50.54(f),
       The lack of technical justification supporting the elimination of required modifications,
       The improper use of SPRA results without applying them to plant safety decisions, and
       Continued procedural deficiencies, including the absence of NRC approval for
       deviations from the established seismic reevaluation framework.

Importantly, Palisades has not yet restarted, and no confirmed startup schedule has been
established. As a result, the issues identified in both the original petition and this supplement
remain timely and actionable, and NRC enforcement action can still be taken prior to fuel load
or entry into Mode 6.

The requested actions in the original petition remain unchanged and are further supported by
the information provided in this supplement.

Please confirm receipt of this supplement and advise if additional information is needed.

Sincerely,
Alan Blind
 1000 West Shawnee Road
Baroda, Michigan 49101
Email: a.alan.blind@gmail.com
Phone: 269-303-6396
 SUPPLEMENT TO 10 CFR § 2.206
PETITION
(Seismic Reevaluation Noncompliance – Palisades Nuclear Plant)

Submitted by:
Alan Blind


I. PURPOSE OF THIS SUPPLEMENT
This supplement is submitted to update the record based on Holtec Palisades, LLC’s most recent
seismic submittal (March 25, 2026) and to clarify that:

  •    The issues raised in the original Petition remain unresolved, and
  •    Newly submitted information by Holtec introduces additional regulatory de ciencies, and
  •    The Palisades Nuclear Plant has not yet restarted, and no con rmed startup schedule has
       been established.
Because restart has not occurred, the NRC retains full authority—and obligation—to ensure
compliance prior to fuel load and entry into Mode 6.

This supplement also identi es a fundamental contradiction in the licensing basis related to Tank
T-81. The originally required modi cation to achieve HCLPF capacity greater than RLGM was
cancelled in 2016 based on the stated intent to use insights from a future Seismic Probabilistic
Risk Assessment (SPRA) to determine appropriate actions. However, in its March 25, 2026
submittal, Holtec states that SPRA results will not be used to initiate structural design changes.
As a result, neither the original deterministic requirement nor the replacement SPRA-based
evaluation framework has been satis ed.


II. STATUS UPDATE: NO RESTART AND NO
APPROVED SCHEDULE
Holtec has not restarted Palisades, and the timeline for restart remains uncertain.

This fact is critical:

  •     The plant remains in a pre-operational state, and
  •     The NRC retains the ability to enforce compliance before irreversible licensing actions
        occur, and
  •     The Petition is therefore ripe and not moot, as the requested relief (preventing premature
        restart) remains fully actionable.

           III. HOLTEC’S SUBMITTAL DOES NOT RESOLVE
          PETITION ISSUES
          Holtec’s March 25, 2026 submittal claims completion of certain seismic activities, including:

            •     Submission of a Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment (SPRA)
            •     Completion of walkdowns and HCLPF evaluations
            •     Closure of previously deferred commitments
          However, these actions do not resolve the core violations identi ed in the Petition, and in several
          cases, con rm them.


          IV. FAILURE TO IMPLEMENT REQUIRED
          STRUCTURAL MODIFICATIONS (T-81) AND
          RESULTING REGULATORY DEFICIENCIES
          Holtec’s March 25, 2026 submittal fails to provide any technical basis for the cancellation of the
          committed seismic modi cation to Tank T-81 and fails to satisfy the conditions under which that
          cancellation was originally justi ed. The original 10 CFR § 50.54(f) response established a clear
          requirement that T-81 achieve a High Con dence of Low Probability of Failure (HCLPF)
          capacity greater than the Review Level Ground Motion (RLGM).

          Although Entergy later cancelled this modi cation in its April 18, 2016 letter (PNP 2016-022),
          that cancellation was explicitly conditional and premised on the future use of SPRA insights, as
          stated:

          “As the reevaluation of seismic risk process continues, the tank modi cation is no longer
          considered to be prudent… based on… new information being obtained in planning and
          executing a Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment (SPRA).
          As an alternative, ENO will use the insights gained through the performance of the SPRA to
          determine what modi cations, procedure changes, or strategy changes would provide the optimal
          safety improvement.”

          Holtec’s March 25, 2026 submittal explicitly acknowledges this history, stating:

          “Modi cation to Primary Makeup Storage Tank (T-81) was cancelled as documented by
          Reference 7.”

          However, in the same submittal, Holtec states:

          “The SPRA alone will not be used in structural design decision-making. Instead, a deterministic
          approach will continue to be utilized…”

                This creates a direct and irreconcilable contradiction in the licensing basis. The 2016 cancellation
               of the T-81 modi cation was explicitly justi ed on the basis that SPRA insights would be used to
               determine necessary safety improvements. Holtec now rejects the use of SPRA for structural
               design decisions, thereby abandoning the very condition under which the modi cation was
               cancelled.

               Holtec’s submittal neither provides a component-speci c HCLPF evaluation for T-81 nor
               demonstrates that the tank meets the original seismic performance requirement. As a result,
               Holtec has neither implemented the original required modi cation nor ful lled the alternative
               SPRA-based evaluation framework that replaced it.

               This de ciency is not isolated but instead reveals a broader pattern in Holtec’s submittal that
               undermines the regulatory intent of the post-Fukushima seismic framework. Holtec’s approach
               effectively replaces speci c, enforceable licensing basis commitments with generalized
               conclusions derived from high-level evaluations. In doing so, Holtec avoids demonstrating
               compliance with discrete requirements—such as the HCLPF capacity obligation for T-81—and
               instead relies on global assertions that no signi cant vulnerabilities were identi ed. This
               substitution is inconsistent with the structure of the 50.54(f) process, which requires that
               identi ed commitments be either ful lled as written or formally revised through NRC-approved
               mechanisms.

               Further, Holtec’s submittal con rms that the SPRA and associated walkdowns were not used to
               drive plant modi cations, as originally intended under NRC-endorsed NEI guidance. By
               explicitly disconnecting SPRA results from design or safety decisions, Holtec renders the SPRA
               process functionally inert and fails to satisfy the requirement that seismic risk insights be applied
               to ensure plant safety.

               The de ciencies associated with T-81 therefore re ect a compounded regulatory failure: the
               licensing basis transitioned from a deterministic requirement (modify T-81 to meet HCLPF >
               RLGM) to a risk-informed requirement (evaluate and determine necessary actions using SPRA).
               Holtec has satis ed neither.

               This failure is further compounded by Holtec’s prior proposal to defer seismic activities until
               after restart without NRC approval. Although certain evaluations have now been completed, they
               were not performed in the required sequence, nor were their results used to satisfy the underlying
               licensing basis obligations.

               Accordingly, the unresolved status of the T-81 commitment—combined with Holtec’s broader
               failure to properly implement, apply, and, where necessary, formally revise seismic requirements
               —constitutes a continuing violation of the Palisades licensing basis and the 10 CFR § 50.54(f)
               framework. This violation remains actionable and must be addressed prior to any authorization
               for fuel load or entry into Mode 6.


               V. NON-CURABLE SEQUENCE VIOLATION

 The original Petition demonstrated that Holtec intended to restart Palisades prior to completion
of required seismic activities.

Holtec has now completed these activities—but only after pursuing restart.

Certain regulatory requirements are sequence-dependent and must be completed before operation
—not retroactively. These include SPRA completion, application of SPRA insights, completion
of walkdowns, and NRC review of nal submittals.

Completion after the fact does not cure the original violation.


VI. FAILURE TO OBTAIN NRC APPROVAL FOR
SCHEDULE DEVIATION
Holtec previously proposed to defer seismic activities until after restart without obtaining NRC
approval.

This procedural violation remains unresolved.


VII. CURRENT REGULATORY POSTURE REQUIRES
NRC ACTION
Because Palisades has not restarted:

  •   The NRC retains full authority to enforce compliance prior to fuel load
Allowing restart would undermine the enforceability of the 50.54(f) process and the post-
Fukushima seismic framework.

IX. CONCLUSION
Holtec’s most recent submittal con rms that required safety determinations have not been
completed and that licensing basis commitments have not been satis ed or properly revised.
